facts.fact: 邻居的地下室和她的一模一样：刷白的墙、光裸的地板、墙上那道几乎藏不住的门，只是左右相反；连气味都一样
facts.anchor: Her basement had the same whitewashed walls as mine. The same bare floor. The same barely concealed door in the wall, only flipped, of course. It even smelled the same.

facts.fact: 三个结：三场考验
facts.anchor: Three knots. Three challenges.

facts.fact: 和 Callie-Ann 谈过之后，她本以为会遇到更多让人暴怒的时刻
facts.anchor: After my chat with Callie-Ann, I’d expected a lot more… rage-inducing moments.

facts.fact: 可到目前为止没有一次让她气到那种程度：悲伤是有的，恐惧肯定有，骇然也肯定有——但气到要发疯？
facts.anchor: But none of the interactions so far had made me that angry. Sad, yes. Terrified, definitely. Horrified, most certainly. But angry to the point of snapping?

facts.fact: 她走进一间亮堂的现代办公室的门厅：玻璃隔断、怪趣家具。可不是随便哪间现代办公室
facts.anchor: I stepped into the foyer of a bright modern office, all glass dividing walls and funky furniture. But not just any modern office.

facts.fact: 那里摆着她那位总监喜欢的橙色百合
facts.anchor: There were the same orange lilies the director liked.

facts.fact: 她一直以为每个人都私下和她一样不快乐，只是更会藏
facts.anchor: I’d always assumed that everyone was secretly just as unhappy as I was, only they were better at hiding it.

facts.fact: 回头看，那位秘书一直对她很好；开发组也从没回避跟她聊天。也许她只是太专注于自己的苦，没看见
facts.anchor: Come to think of it, she’d always been nice to me. The Dev Team, too, had never seemed shy about chatting with me. Maybe I’d been a little too focused on my own misery to see it.

facts.fact: 总监具备她心目中现代职业女性应有的一切，也具备她所没有的一切
facts.anchor: She was everything I thought a modern career woman should be. And everything I was not.

facts.fact: 总监宣布："明星奖时间到！幸运儿有五十镑电子券。"
facts.anchor: “It’s Star Awards time!” the director announced. “And I’ve got fifty quid in digital vouchers for our lucky winner.”

facts.fact: 念到她的提名时，总监挑眉、眯眼看纸条、靠上 Alan 的升降桌："最后是 CRM 部的 Tamsin，因为——开发了一个用标签自动填充客户邮件的模板。"
facts.anchor: “And finally, we have”—she raised her eyebrows in surprise—“Tamsin from CRM Services for”—she squinted at the paper and leaned on Alan’s standing desk—“developing a template to automatically populate customer emails with tags.”

facts.fact: 她把每个词都念得像陌生菜单上的异国菜名，或某种早被遗忘的蜥蜴的分类名
facts.anchor: She said each word as if it were the name of an exotic dish on an unfamiliar menu, or the taxonomy of some long-forgotten lizard.

facts.fact: 总监耸耸肩："管它是什么呢。"
facts.anchor: The director shrugged. “Whatever that is.”

facts.fact: "那么，本月明星奖颁给……Felicity！"
facts.anchor: “In which case, this month’s Star Award goes to… Felicity!

facts.fact: 她对总监说："我看见你了，我明白。你……那么努力地跟年轻人套近乎。衣服、头发、指甲。"
facts.anchor: “I see you and I understand,” I said. “You, uh… the way you try so hard to pal about with the younger ones. The clothes, the hair, the nails.

facts.fact: "你从没意识到，你是在身后把梯子往上收。"
facts.anchor: You never realised you were pulling the ladder up behind you.”

facts.fact: "我不知道你当年有多担心。我们都担心。"
facts.anchor: I don’t know how much you must have worried. We all worried.”

facts.fact: "你没弄懂我做的东西。你说得好像我们是在往邮件里塞标签。你弄错了。你根本不知道那是什么。"
facts.anchor: “You didn’t understand what I’d made. You said it like we were putting tags into emails. You got it wrong. You didn’t know what it was.

facts.fact: "你不懂，而'不懂'让你害怕。所以你就开了个玩笑。"
facts.anchor: You didn’t understand and it scared you not to understand. So, you made a joke instead.”

facts.fact: 她伸手去拿线，说："这从来都跟我无关。你——"
facts.anchor: “It was never about me. You—”

facts.fact: 但她错了：这件事恰恰跟她有关
facts.anchor: But I was wrong. This was exactly about me.

facts.fact: 她看见自己出现在人群后面——不是旁观的那个她，是当年的那个她
facts.anchor: I watched as I appeared at the back of the crowd. Not the me-watching-this-happen. The me-back-then.

facts.fact: 那张总监随手把手穿过去、手指正搭在梁交叉处的桌子——X 标出的位置
facts.anchor: The desk the director had carelessly threaded her hand through, fingers resting right at the crossing of those beams, the X that marks the spot.

facts.fact: 她看着自己抓住安全栓
facts.anchor: I watched myself grab the safety latch.

facts.fact: 她看着自己的脸，没有表情，嘴抿成一条细线
facts.anchor: I watched my face, expressionless, my mouth a thin line.
